s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with radiating pain to the left thigh, accompanied by nausea, vomiting, and a palpable mass in the left buttock area, suggesting an obstructive and potentially strangulated hernia
salient_findings: Severe crampy pains in hypogastrium radiating down the back of the left thigh
Painful, non-reducible, tender mass in the left buttock area
History of intermittent abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting
key_facts: 45-year-old woman presented with severe abdominal pain
Pain radiates to the back of the left thigh
Nausea and vomiting accompanying the pain
Palpable, painful mass in the left buttock area
Mass measures 10 cm × 8 cm × 8 cm
Abdomen is soft with epigastrium tenderness and rebounding pain
Absence of intestinal gurgling sounds
History of calculous cholecystitis and cesarean delivery
Patient appears dehydrated and poorly nourished
Knee-flexed position due to pain
Intestinal obstruction and gallstone seen on abdominal X-ray
Incarcerated bowel loops beneath left gluteal muscles on ultrasonography
CT examination shows seroperitoneum, pneumoperitoneum, and low intestinal obstruction
